preserved_literal_source_notation: The group symbol: the exercise prints a blackboard-bold capital Z followed by a script-size circled dot set above the line, and physical p. 106 uses the same two-glyph setting. It is transcribed as \Z^{\odot}, i.e. Z with odot as a superscript. The base letter comes from the root session's own full-resolution viewing of physical p. 251, recorded in the reader as such; it does not come from this session's pixel reading, and it cannot come from the text layer, where the letter is an unmapped byte of a math-italic font with no Unicode map and the circled dot extracts as the ordinary circled-dot character. The geometry instrument independently confirms the relative setting on both pages (base frak 9.45 / 10.5 pt, star 6.3 / 7.35 pt, raised 0.83 / 1.19-1.20 pt, x offset 7.10 / 8.33-8.34 pt) but cannot decide the base letter.

The subscript pair: the exercise prints p_{2n}(o,o) and the Comment prints p_n(o,o). Measured from spans, on p. 251 the '2' and 'n' are 6.3 pt with baseline drop 3.9 pt (size ratio 0.667, y-spread 0.06) against a 9.45 pt body, and on p. 637 the 'n' is 6.3 pt with drop 2.88 pt (ratio 0.75, y-spread 0.0) against an 8.4 pt body. Both are baseline subscripts, neither is an exponent, and the two literals are kept side by side without synchronisation. This matches the adjudication's first residue, which keeps both because the estimate is uniform in n so 2n is a relabelling.

The exponent: n^{1/3} on p. 251 has its 1, solidus and 3 all at 6.3 pt with baseline drop -0.95 pt, i.e. raised; on p. 637 the same setting gives -1.36 pt. The instrument therefore distinguishes the genuine script-size fraction exponent from the subscripts above, and n^{1/3} is transcribed as printed in both places.

The constants: the Comment's 'for some constant c', its c_1, and the exercise's C are all kept as printed and none is identified with another. The ceiling \lceil n/r^{2}\rceil and the interval [-2r,2r] are transcribed literally. This matches the adjudication's third residue: the absorption of the ceiling into n/r^2 + 1 and the assembly of C from c and c_1 are mechanical and are not written into the reader.

The block-confinement estimate: the Comment asserts a uniform lower bound 'for some constant c' and does not derive that constant inside the Comment. The reader keeps the assertion as printed and neither derives the constant nor replaces it. This matches the adjudication's second residue: the confinement estimate is asserted in the book's own style for such estimates, and every asked target is covered.

The external attribution: the Comment closes 'See Pittet and Saloff-Coste (1999)'. The reader keeps that sentence and reprints the book's own bibliography entry for it, with the explicit statement that the work was not obtained or consulted. The attribution is the author's, and no content from that work is inserted.

limitations: No pixel inspection of any page was performed by this session; the conclusion rests on text layers and on geometric measurement of span sizes, baselines and fonts only. The four 150 dpi renderings under render/ are stored but were not viewed. The one exception in evidence, not in method, is the group symbol: its base letter is the root session's full-resolution viewing of physical p. 251, recorded as the root's reading and not as this session's.

The PDF text layer of this source has systematic artefacts that a naive substring test misreads: Latin ligatures are decomposed ('de ned', 'su ces', 'in mum'), the sans-serif V of the vertex set is dropped, super- and subscripts are flattened, the wreath-product operator extracts as 'Y', and the delimiter fonts encode the big parentheses as control code points. In this source's text layer two control bytes (0x0A and 0x0B) sit at the fence around (Psi_j, X_j) on p. 251, and in the reader's own text layer six control characters appear on pages 2 and 3 (four and two). All are Type1 delimiter-font encodings surfacing in extraction; none is a missing glyph and none is a rendering defect, and replacement characters are zero everywhere.

Because super- and subscripts are flattened by extraction, exponent and index placement in the reader is not verified by these instruments; it is verified only insofar as LaTeX produced it and latexmk reported no error. The source-side subscript-versus-exponent question is therefore settled from the source page geometry, and the reader-side setting from the TeX source read in full.
